name: Acrylic & High-Gloss Surfaces
tagline: Depth, reflection and the finish clients notice first
description: Everything in this section exists to bounce light. Acrylic and PET panels give kitchens and wardrobes a mirror depth that laminate cannot reach — at a price, and with a maintenance conversation the client should have before you specify it.

materials.name: Acrylic sheet
materials.blurb: Cast acrylic panel with a glass-like reflection
materials.description: A solid cast acrylic layer bonded to board gives the deepest gloss available in modular joinery. Reads almost like lacquered glass, and unlike gloss laminate it can be polished if it scratches.

materials.name: Acrylic laminate
materials.blurb: Acrylic-faced laminate — most of the depth, less of the cost
materials.description: A thinner acrylic layer on a laminate carrier. Visually close to full acrylic at arm's length and a common value engineering swap when the kitchen budget tightens.

materials.name: PET sheet
materials.blurb: Recyclable gloss panel with better scratch behaviour than acrylic
materials.description: PET gives a comparable shine to acrylic with a harder, more scratch-tolerant face and a stronger recycling story. Increasingly specified where sustainability is on the client brief.

materials.name: High-gloss panel (pre-laminated)
materials.blurb: Board that arrives finished on both faces, edges banded
materials.description: A ready-to-fit panel — gloss face, balanced back, matching 2 mm band. Removes the pressing and banding steps from a tight programme and guarantees a factory-flat surface.

materials.name: Anti-fingerprint panel
materials.blurb: Matte or gloss surface treated to shrug off smudges
materials.description: A nano-coating that stops fingerprints registering on dark surfaces. On a handle-less charcoal kitchen this is not a luxury — it is the difference between a photograph and a smear.

materials.name: Matte acrylic
materials.blurb: The softness of suede with the depth of acrylic
materials.description: Acrylic's solid colour depth in a low-sheen finish — currently the most requested premium kitchen surface. Pairs well with fluted timber and stone counters.

materials.name: Metallic acrylic
materials.blurb: Metal-effect gloss for bars, retail and statement units
materials.description: Champagne, bronze and gunmetal acrylics with a mirrored metallic depth. Strong in small doses — a bar front or a single wardrobe bay — and overwhelming across a whole room.
